title: Complete move narratives constrained by one fixed historical board-game rulebook
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A complete passage may encode a complete legal move narrative: one shared piece/action/location lexicon must replay every move from an independently fixed initial position and produce the stated final position. This is a creative semantic hypothesis, not an observed Voynich game identification or a numerical-route repair.

design.meaning: Operational readings such as move the knight from this square to that square, capture that piece, or the king is threatened. Piece roles are constrained by legal transitions, occupancy, turn alternation and resulting state rather than arbitrary assigned word glosses.
design.fixed_system: Before any fit, freeze ONE independently sourced historical game variant, its full legal rules and starting setup. Modern chess rules are not silently projected backward. The intended candidate is a chess-family move narrative; historical variant and literal notation remain unestablished prerequisites.
design.complete_record: One entire independently bounded passage is one move narrative with all moves consumed. Require each statement to encode actor, departure, arrival, capture/no-capture and explicit final-state claims under a fixed finite grammar. No omitted moves, freely chosen starting board, per-move coordinates, clause exceptions or dictionary values unique to one occurrence.
design.shared_writing_rule: One global injective primitive code for piece types, actions and symbolic board-file/rank values; complete statements use the same frozen serializer throughout. Do not infer piece identity from EVA resemblance or adopt a numerical code from the currently tested division route. The serializer is not yet selected.
design.joint_constraint: Each complete statement changes the state consumed by every following statement. A captured piece cannot move later; a blocked path cannot be traversed; alternation and threat rules must agree across the complete game. Multiple complete games must share one code and the frozen setup.
design.positive_output: Retain all legal global keys and board symmetries. Claim a conditional complete game reading only if every surviving key gives the same move/action/piece interpretation of every statement, modulo explicitly reported whole-board symmetries. Predict the whole terminal board or a separately withheld complete continuation before viewing it. Multiple keys or unspecific legal games are not translation.
design.strongest_falsifier: Any definite move requiring an absent piece, occupied forbidden destination or impossible legal transition under every retained key rejects that full reading. A fit that needs an unrecorded extra move also fails.
design.symmetry_limit: Board rotation/reflection, player-color interchange and historical nomenclature can remain unidentified. Rule legality alone does not identify names of people, geographic places or a natural-language sentence. Require independent orientation/color evidence before reporting named square/color values.
missing_inputs: No independently nominated complete Voynich game passage or board state.
No frozen historical rule variant or notation/statement contract.
No demonstrated capacity to distinguish true move narratives from alternative complete prose under this expressive model.
design.predecessors: Bounded idea search found no chess/game-move card; route-check returned generic register matches, not an established game test. This does not reopen GDT899/908 conditional source-copy codes, numerical multiplication/register exclusions or the current division hypothesis. No image, target artifact, raw TSV or held data accessed.
design.selection: Raw creative successor only; source/method review and separately justified target scope required before experiment selection.
